Switched to a new branch 'research/agent-architecture'
# CLAUDE.md

Team error404.ai at the Atira EHL Challenge ("From RFQ to bid", challenge id `rfq`, event 10 Oct 2026, up to 5 people
per team). The agent lives in `agent/` and is built on the Atira starter kit. Keep the GitHub repo private.

## Status and layout

- `docs/plan.md`: framework decision (pydantic-ai on Qwen, no LangGraph, no browser-agent framework), module layout,
  site scouting notes and the roadmap v0 to v5. Read it first. Its scouting notes describe public-1 only: they inform
  generic helpers, they must never become hardcoded paths, labels, values or prompt text (the private final run uses
  other software, layouts and data).
- `agent/`: starter kit (`run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py`, `agent.py` with the `solve()` stub) plus the new harness
  modules `llm.py`, `extract.py`, `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `tracing.py`. Planned, not yet present: `roles.py`,
  `evidence.py`, `calc.py`, `submit.py`. `agent.json` has no `browsers` key yet (default 1; the plan wants 4).
- `dev/smoke.py`: the v0 check (one worker per site logs in and reads a page). From the repo root:
  `eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/smoke.py [siteId ...]`
- Next: finish v0, then v1 (a signed, eligible bid), then v2 to v4 for field points. Use `git status` and
  `atira status` for the current state; do not trust dated numbers in this file.

## Platform docs (source of truth; re-read, they change)

Base `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai`. Public pages (home, start, challenge, leaderboard, team profiles) are also
Markdown via `.md`; docs are `/docs/<name>.md`.

- `/start.md`, `/challenges/rfq.md` (29 bid rules, answer schema), `/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md`
- `/docs/fair-play.md`, `scoring.md`, `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `building-an-agent.md`, `cli.md`, `api.md`,
  `mcp.md`, `faq.md`, `demo-day.md`; `/openapi.json`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` (all docs in one file)
- Announcements need a token: `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/v1/announcements`
- Submission deadline and prizes are not in the docs: ask the organizers. Demo day: best teams run live on stage, so
  keep a one-line start command (`atira test-run ./agent`) and a fallback recording.

The scouting logins are deliberately NOT stored here: run `atira scout`. Never write them, or anything copied from
the sites, into code, prompts, fixtures, notes or fallbacks.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer rejects or flags these)

- No hardcoded scenario values (tender refs, material numbers, prices, discounts, logins, TANs), not even as defaults,
  fallbacks or in prompts. Facts the brief states for every scenario (e.g. the sales director's mailbox) are fine.
- No pre-solving, by you or an AI assistant, put into the package. Hand-derived expectations stay outside `agent/`.
- Must be agentic: a model chooses where to go, what to search and what matters. Rejected: a fixed click path (model
  unused or only a fallback), or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation.
  Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate,
  validate, retry, fill forms. Several agents and parallel browsers are fine.
- Only the platform API, the four sites and the model proxy; no local models; no own browsers in the sandbox (use the
  provided 1 to 4, tabs and contexts are free).
- Do not write notes meant to steer the reviewer. Outcomes: passed; flagged (runs, but hidden from the leaderboard
  until an organizer passes it); rejected (no runs).

## The task and its traps

One signed bid, entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. Site ids are
public-1 names; the private set renames and re-splits sites, so never branch code on siteId, URL or layout.

| Site | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Tender portal | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (the hub: quantity changes, withdrawals, scoped spec amendments, Konditionsgruppe, packaging, commitment and setup-pool keys), configurator |
| Supplier portal | Buyer's spec and revisions (oldest shown first; use the one marked current) |
| ERP | Materials and status, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity and scales, pieces per carton, allocation mass |
| Webmail | Director's discount approval, TAN, authority mails (look-alikes, superseded, archive) |

Read all 29 rules in `challenges/rfq.md` before writing prompts or tools. Highest-impact traps:

- **Authority and time (21):** per key, the latest record dated no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender
  reference, from the right sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation + bidder mailbox domain). Future-dated and
  unrelated records never apply; a failed condition does not revive an older record.
- **no_bid (3, 8, 16):** if any position has no exactly matching active material (after amendments and the "nutzbarer
  Weg" derivation, rule 20), send `no_bid`, no positions, `total_net` 0 (schema still requires `discount_percent`; a
  conditional approval means 0 %). Omitting positions is not a substitute (rule 9).
- **Sign and submit:** saving alone scores nothing. Partial bids use "Position auslassen" and are still signed.
- **Per position vs per material:** price scales per position; stock pooled per material (15); delivery commitments
  per position, only if the material matches and pooled demand is within the inclusive ceiling (24).
- **Rounding:** HALF_UP, at the steps the rules name: FX-converted base price to cents (22), discount threshold and
  bonus aggregate to cents (16, 26), then the final unit price once from unrounded per-piece components (27).
  Breakdown fields are reports, not inputs. Bonus split: largest remainders (26); setup pool: the cent-allocation rule
  stated in the Ruestpools mail (25).
- **Reporting:** `surcharge_per_unit` is before discount and covers mass surcharge plus ordinary and allocated setup;
  setup and packaging are never discounted; blank = unanswered, `0.00` = known zero; `rebate_total` is per position.
- **Conditional discount (16):** threshold uses undiscounted scale prices, no surcharge or setup, inclusive; on failure
  0 %, never an older approval. Metal index: the rate whose window contains the scenario date (28).
- Positions are matched by number; extras or duplicates cost one position's share; money is compared to the cent.

## Runs, ranking, winning

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

- Test run (`atira test-run ./agent --follow`): 2 h, public data, shows per-part points, never on the leaderboard.
  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's
  `run.seconds_left` helps); platform docs only say "about a minute". A run without an answer scores 0.
- Setup has network and 5 min (untimed), but no run variables or secrets, and nothing it starts survives. The timed run
  reaches only the platform, sites and model proxy (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, honour it in custom clients). Send your own
  User-Agent (default Python agents get 403 "Error 1010").
- `agent.json`: `setup`, `run`, `models` (list every hosted model used, e.g. `["qwen","clef"]`), `browsers` 1 to 4.
  Package: 20 MB compressed and uncompressed, 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, `.gitignore` honoured, no secrets inside.
  Own model keys are team secrets (names: capitals, digits, underscore, letter first, max 20, no platform names).
- Order: eligible (right tender reference), then quality 0 to 100, then lower cost x time (floors $0.01, 1 s). A wrong
  bid/no_bid decision costs quality, not eligibility (75 of 100 in a no_bid case). Weights: rule 29.
- Winners: private-dataset final run of our LATEST submission that PASSED review (not the best), then public
  leaderboard, then elegance. So: never tune to public-1; every passing `atira submit` replaces the final candidate,
  even a worse one, so confirm with the team first. `atira final --best-of 3` (before the final starts) allows three
  attempts (own-key cost up to 3x); private runs show no score breakdown.
- Models: hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`QWEN_BASE_URL/KEY`, 32 concurrent) and Clef (`CLEF_*`, 16 concurrent) are free
  but add a SIMULATED price to run cost; own-key calls are metered at provider prices through the proxy. Measured
  Qwen behaviour (thinking flag, schema cold start, caching) is in `docs/plan.md`.

## Dev loop

```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh    # CLI; the installer provides Node 24 if missing
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && atira login           # `atira upgrade` if a command is unknown
(cd agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium)
atira models proxy                       # terminal 1 (port 8765)
eval "$(atira scout --env)"              # terminal 2: scouting logins + model vars
(cd agent && uv run --no-sync python agent.py)   # local run, nothing submitted
(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)

```

Debugging: `atira logs <run> --follow`, `atira status [id]`, `atira package <id> --out dir`, `atira cancel <run>`; every
command takes `--json`. `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp` gives `diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`,
`run_screenshot`, `compare_runs` and more (`mcp.md`). Use the score breakdown to localise errors (zero surcharge
points can come from mass surcharge, setup or metal index inputs). A cancelled scored run ends its submission (ignored
by the leaderboard), so you may resubmit. Missing "OpenAI key" 401s mean no provider key arrived (team secret).
On macOS, python.org Python needs `Install Certificates.command` or `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

## Team conventions

- Git: commit author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`; imperative subject of at most 50 characters, body as short `-`
  bullets; no attribution trailers (no Co-Authored-By, no session links); never stage anything under `.claude/`;
  never push or open a PR without asking first.
- Never put real credentials, personal data or site values in tests, fixtures, docs or comments; invent placeholders.
# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

## Docs

- How a run works: `$API/docs/run-contract.md`
- Building an agent: `$API/docs/building-an-agent.md`
- Fair play, the rules: `$API/docs/fair-play.md`

## Tests

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
```
{
  "setup": ["uv", "sync"],
  "run": ["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "agent.py"],
  "models": ["qwen"]
}
"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import browsers
import models  # noqa: F401  models.ask_qwen, models.ask_clef: see models.py
import run as contract


async def solve(task: dict, page) -> dict | None:
    """TODO: your agent goes here.

    `task` is the run: task["brief"] (the task and its rules), task["access"] (each website's url and login),
    task["submission"] (where the answer goes) and task["answer_schema"]. `page` is a Playwright page in browser 1.

    For an "api" submission, return the answer and main() submits it. For a "site" submission, enter the answer on
    that website yourself, then return None.

    Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `contract.seconds_left(task)` says how many are left. Every part
    of the answer scores on its own, so stop and submit your best answer about a minute before the end; an answer
    that comes too late scores 0.
    """
    return None


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright)  # more browsers: browsers.connect(playwright, 1), ...
        answer = await solve(task, page)
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit: build your agent in solve() in agent.py", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page
"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:
        response = await client.post(os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide", json=body,
                                     headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["answers"]["q"]["noul"]
"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

1	# Getting started: from sign-in to your first scored run
2	
3	How to sign in, set up and test your agent, and get it on the leaderboard. Limits and scoring are at the bottom.
4	
5	Fastest start: point Claude Code or Codex at this site. Paste this, and it installs the CLI, connects itself, and helps you build, test and submit:
6	
7	```text
8	Read https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt, then set us up and help us build, test and submit an agent for this challenge.
9	```
10	
11	Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start) · The challenge: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)
12	
13	## What you're building
14	
15	Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
16	
17	## Your first test run
18	
19	Seven steps. The first five get your agent running against the websites. Step 6 tests it in the sandbox; step 7 puts it on the leaderboard.
20	
21	### 1. Sign in and form a team
22	
23	[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.
24	
25	### 2. Install the CLI and sign in
26	
27	The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).
28	
29	macOS and Linux:
30	
31	```sh
32	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
33	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
34	atira login
35	```
36	
37	Windows, in PowerShell:
38	
39	```powershell
40	irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex
41	atira login
42	```
43	
44	Optional: connect the coding agent you use (one line each):
45	
46	```sh
47	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
48	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
49	```
50	
51	### 3. Scout the websites yourself
52	
53	Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored. Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)
54	
55	| Website | URL | Username | Password |
56	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
57	| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
58	| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
59	| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
60	| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |
61	
62	### 4. Choose your starting point
63	
64	Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.
65	
66	macOS and Linux:
67	
68	```sh
69	mkdir my-agent
70	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
71	```
72	
73	Windows, in PowerShell:
74	
75	```powershell
76	mkdir my-agent
77	curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
78	tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
79	```
80	
81	### 5. Develop locally
82	
83	You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).
84	
85	macOS and Linux:
86	
87	```sh
88	cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
89	eval "$(atira scout --env)"
90	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
91	```
92	
93	Windows, in PowerShell:
94	
95	```powershell
96	cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
97	atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
98	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
99	```
100	
101	Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).
102	
103	### 6. Test in the sandbox
104	
105	The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.
106	
107	```sh
108	atira test-run .
109	```
110	
111	### 7. Submit
112	
113	A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).
114	
115	```sh
116	atira submit .
117	```
118	
119	## Unlimited Inference
120	
121	We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
122	
123	### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
124	
125	#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.
126	
127	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
128	- **Simulated pricing:**
129	  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
130	  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
131	  - Cache writes: Free
132	  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
133	- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)
134	
135	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
136	
137	```python
138	import os
139	from openai import OpenAI
140	
141	qwen = OpenAI(
142	    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
143	    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
144	)
145	reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
146	    model="qwen",
147	    messages=[{
148	        "role": "user",
149	        "content": "Which button submits?",
150	    }],
151	)
152	```
153	
154	### Cloudflare Clef
155	
156	A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.
157	
158	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
159	- **Simulated pricing:**
160	  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
161	  - Output: Not priced
162	
163	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
164	
165	```sh
166	curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
167	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
168	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
169	  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
170	  "questions": {"next": {
171	    "type": "choice",
172	    "instructions": "What next?",
173	    "criteria": {
174	      "retry": "Retry the request",
175	      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
176	```
177	
178	In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.
179	
180	```sh
181	atira login   # once per computer
182	atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
183	export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
184	export QWEN_API_KEY=local
185	export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
186	export CLEF_API_KEY=local
187	```
188	
189	Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.
190	
191	If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.
192	
193	## Limits
194	
195	What every scored run gets.
196	
197	| Rule | What it means |
198	| --- | --- |
199	| Scored run | 20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team. |
200	| Setup and network | Setup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy. |
201	| Models | Bring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. |
202	| Browsers | At most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs. |
203	| Sandbox | 4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo. |
204	| Package | Up to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup. |
205	| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
206	| Team | Up to 5 people. |
207	
208	## How you're scored
209	
210	Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.
211	
212	- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
213	- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
214	
215	Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.
216	
217	Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.
218	
219	On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.
220	
221	## Public and private data
222	
223	The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
224	
225	## Using a coding agent?
226	
227	Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.
228	
229	Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.
230	
231	```sh
232	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp   # Claude Code
233	codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp    # Codex
234	```
235

1959	# Answers and scoring
1960	
1961	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
1962	
1963	Each challenge defines its answer format and how quality is scored; the platform measures cost and time and
1964	ranks everyone the same way. Test runs, scored submissions and the scouting logins use the public dataset (the
1965	websites as you see them, with scenario `public-1`), and the leaderboard ranks those results. The correct answer
1966	isn't published; your system has to work it out from the websites. When the hackathon ends, a [final run](#final-run)
1967	on a private dataset weighs most when we pick the [winners](#winners).
1968	
1969	## Per run
1970	
1971	- **Quality** (0 to 100): how right the answer is, by the challenge's scorer.
1972	- **Eligible:** whether the answer meets the challenge's mandatory criteria. For RFQ: the right tender reference;
1973	  a wrong decision (bid or no_bid) costs quality points instead.
1974	- **Cost:** the run's LLM usage, priced per model, in USD.
1975	- **Time:** from the start of your run command to your accepted answer.
1976	
1977	A malformed answer is rejected with a `400` and does not end the run. A well-formed answer is final, even if it
1978	is wrong. A run without an answer scores quality 0 and is not eligible.
1979	
1980	## Leaderboard
1981	
1982	Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset and is scored; one run per submission
1983	keeps your model bill down. A submission appears once its run has finished and review is passed; reviewer flags await organizer approval. Each team is ranked by its best
1984	complete submission. The API reports them in its `median_*` fields; with one run per submission, that is
1985	the run's own value.
1986	
1987	1. Eligible before ineligible.
1988	2. Higher quality.
1989	3. Lower cost × time: the submission's cost in USD times its time, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time
1990	   as at least 1 second. Cost and time weigh the same: halving your model bill counts as much as halving your run
1991	   time, and among free runs the faster one wins.
1992	4. The submission ID, when everything above is equal.
1993	
1994	On the leaderboard's plot, each team is a dot, quality against cost or time; the dotted line is the Pareto front,
1995	the teams no other eligible team beats on both.
1996	
1997	Test runs and scored runs on the public scenario `public-1` show your team the points for each part of the answer,
1998	never the expected values. Runs on the private dataset show quality, eligibility, cost and time without a breakdown.
1999	
2000	## Final run
2001	
2002	When the hackathon ends, the organizers run every team's latest submission that passed review (organizers resolve outstanding reviewer flags before the final run starts; rejected ones don't count) once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it, and each run's brief states the bid rules. It ranks in the same order as above. Build an agent that works the
2003	answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
2004	
2005	## Winners
2006	
2007	We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order:
2008	
2009	1. Performance on the private dataset (the final run).
2010	2. Performance on the public dataset (the leaderboard).
2011	3. The elegance of the system.
2012	
2013	It is the latest submission, not the best one: your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
2014	latest one that passed review goes into the final run. The final run's results stay with the organizers until they
2015	publish them. Then the leaderboard shows the final results, tagged "Private dataset · final", with each team's
2016	public-dataset result and its change in rank beside them, and the public-dataset board stays at `$API/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public` (Markdown:
2017	`leaderboard.md?dataset=public`; API: `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public`).
2018	
2019	## RFQ scoring
2020	
2021	The brief states the calculation rules. Each position has four optional fields that earn independent points:
2022	`base_unit_price` (the EUR scale price per piece before discount), `surcharge_per_unit` (material surcharge plus
2023	ordinary and allocated setup cost per piece, before discount), `packaging_per_unit`, and `rebate_total` (the
2024	project-bonus credit for the **entire position**). Leave a field blank if unanswered; enter zero for a known zero.
2025	The same calculation rules and answer format apply to the public and private datasets. You can also explicitly
2026	omit unfinished positions in the form; completed fields retain their credit. You must sign and submit to score.
2027	
2028	| Part (a bid) | Points |
2029	| --- | --- |
2030	| Decision | 5 |
2031	| Tender reference | 5 |
2032	| Discount percent | 5 |
2033	| Total net (to the cent, consistent with the positions) | 5 |
2034	| Arithmetic (every position, and a total that is their sum) | 5 |
2035	| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (when present) | 5 |
2036	| Dated metal-index check (when present) | 5 |
2037	| Positions (split evenly): material 20 %, quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, project bonus 10 %, unit price 10 %, lead time 10 % | 75 minus the checks above |
2038	
2039	
2040	For a no_bid case: decision 75, tender reference 5, no positions 5, a total of 0 15. A wrong decision costs its
2041	points but leaves the other fields their credit.
2042	
2043	Money is compared to the cent. Positions are matched by their position number; extra or duplicate positions cost
2044	one position's share each.

2046	## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three
2047	
2048	The final runs your latest passed submission on the private set. The default is one attempt.
2049	Before the final run starts, opt in to **Best of 3** on your team page or run
2050	`atira final --best-of 3` (`--best-of 1` opts out). `atira status` shows the choice.
2051	When the final run starts, each team's choice is fixed, including teams still in review.
2052	Opted-in teams get up to three attempts on the same private scenario(s). Your **single best complete attempt**
2053	counts: eligible first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time, with the leaderboard's usual floors.
2054	It is not an average, and a failed attempt does not outweigh a better successful one.
2055	Every attempt is kept. Your team sees its own attempts' logs (private values masked) and, once the organizers publish the final, the results.
2056	Calls using your own model keys can cost up to **3×**. The public leaderboard remains one run per submission
2057	on the public scenario. Review, flags and disqualification work as for any submission.
2058	
2059	Flagged results are hidden from the public leaderboard by default. **Show flagged** on the page (or `?flagged=1` on
2060	the leaderboard API) lists them beside the approved ones, tagged "flagged: waiting for an organizer" and without a
2061	rank, so showing them does not change other ranks. An organizer pass makes a flagged result count normally.

2067	# How a run works
2068	
2069	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
2070	
2071	A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge. It starts with a run token, gives your agent a task and
2072	logins for the challenge's websites, and ends when your agent submits its answer or time runs out. Test runs and
2073	scored runs both run your package in the [sandbox](#scored-run); you develop on your own machine with the scouting
2074	logins.
2075	
2076	## Develop locally, then test in the sandbox
2077	
2078	RFQ has one public scenario, `public-1`: the websites as you see them.
2079	
2080	1. **Develop locally** against the public websites with the scouting logins the organizers publish:
2081	   `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` (in PowerShell: `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`) sets
2082	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the websites and their logins, the JSON a run gets), each website's URL as
2083	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL`, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the `brief`, `access`, `submission` and `answer_schema` of
2084	   `GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` as JSON (`CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` is that address). There is no run token.
2085	   Where the platform hosts models, they need no key: `--env` also exports each one's base URL and key, pointed at
2086	   `atira models proxy` on your computer with `local` as the key, so run `atira login` once, then keep
2087	   `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. Those calls are free, recorded and never ranked. Any other
2088	   provider takes your own key.
2089	   Nothing done with these logins counts.
2090	   A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
2091	2. **Test in the sandbox:** `atira test-run ./my-agent` uploads your package, starts a test run on `public-1` and
2092	   opens its run page live. It runs in the same sandbox as a scored run, but for up to 2 hours instead of 20 minutes (keep it under
2093	   20 to be safe), and the run page shows its
2094	   score with the full breakdown. `atira cancel` stops it early.
2095	
2096	## Inside a run
2097	
2098	1. **Read the task:** `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with the header `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`
2099	   returns:
2100	   - `brief`: the task statement in markdown, with the rules;
2101	   - `access`: one entry per website: `siteId`, `url`, and `credentials` (`username`, `password`);
2102	   - `submission`: where the answer goes: `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` (POST it to that URL) or
2103	     `{"kind": "site", "siteId": ..., "url": ...}` (submit it on that website, e.g. RFQ's configurator);
2104	   - `answer_url` (API submissions only) and `answer_schema` (JSON Schema of the answer);
2105	   - `started_at`, `expires_at`, and what the run has spent on LLM calls so far.
2106	   - `llm_proxy_url`: the model proxy base with this run's token, `llm_providers` and `llm_base_urls` (each
2107	     provider's proxy base), and `llm_env` (the SDK base-URL variables the run step gets).
2108	   Keep the token secret: it is your agent's identity for this run.
2109	2. **Work:** your agent logs into the websites with those credentials and collects what it needs. Its LLM calls
2110	   go through our metering proxy: a hosted model's with the run token its key variable already holds, any other
2111	   provider's with your own key (below).
2112	3. **Answer** through the run's `submission` target. For an `api` target, `POST` the answer as JSON to
2113	   `answer_url` with the same `x-api-key` header. For a `site` target, submit it on that website: the site
2114	   forwards it to the platform, shows the same validation issues in German, and confirms with a receipt.
2115	   - `400` with `issues`: the answer is malformed. Nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running, fix it and send
2116	     it again.
2117	   - `202`: accepted and final. The run ends, the token and the website logins stop working, and a test run
2118	     returns its score and breakdown. Your agent then has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.
2119	
2120	Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live. Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header
2121	(`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
2122	front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.
2123	
2124	## LLM calls
2125	
2126	Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
2127	Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
2128	own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
2129	API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.
2130	
2131	The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:
2132	
2133	```
2134	$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
2135	```
2136	
2137	`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:
2138	
2139	| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
2140	| --- | --- | --- |
2141	| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
2142	| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
2143	| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
2144	| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
2145	| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
2146	| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
2147	| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
2148	| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
2149	| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
2150	| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |
2151	
2152	The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
2153	each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
2154	(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.
2155	
2156	### Your key
2157	
2158	Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
2159	(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
2160	unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
2161	not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.
2162	
2163	With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
2164	`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
2165	as `x-api-key`:
2166	
2167	```python
2168	from openai import OpenAI
2169	
2170	client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
2171	```
2172	
2173	A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
2174	the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:
2175	
2176	```python
2177	import os
2178	from google import genai
2179	
2180	client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
2181	    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
2182	```
2183	
2184	```javascript
2185	import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"
2186	
2187	const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
2188	  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
2189	```
2190	
2191	A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
2192	organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
2193	key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
2194	start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.
2195	
2196	**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
2197	`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
2198	(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
2199	for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
2200	`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
2201	`401`.
2202	
2203	A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
2204	context.
2205	
2206	### How cost is measured
2207	
2208	Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
2209	provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
2210	A model too new for the platform's price list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it, its long-context price
2211	included. An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
2212	`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
2213	that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
2214	a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
2215	providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
2216	chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
2217	an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
2218	early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
2219	endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
2220	fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.
2221	
2222	The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
2223	charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.
2224	
2225	### Team secrets
2226	
2227	Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
2228	`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:
2229	
2230	```sh
2231	curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
2232	  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
2233	curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
2234	curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
2235	```
2236	
2237	Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
2238	Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
2239	cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
2240	`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.

2242	## Scored run
2243	
2244	Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
2245	ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
2246	[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
2247	a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
2248	`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:
2249	
2250	- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
2251	- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
2252	- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
2253	  and the websites.
2254	- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.
2255	
2256	1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
2257	2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
2258	   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
2259	   run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
2260	   never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
2261	   them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
2262	   `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
2263	   right after setup:
2264	
2265	   ```json
2266	   {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
2267	   ```
2268	
2269	   Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
2270	   `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
2271	   whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.
2272	
2273	   **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
2274	   If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
2275	   connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
2276	   then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
2277	   any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
2278	   run that answered keeps its result.
2279	3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.
2280	
2281	| Variable | Value |
2282	| --- | --- |
2283	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
2284	| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
2285	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |

2288	| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
2289	| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
2290	| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google`; set the Gemini SDK's HTTP base URL explicitly as above |
2291	| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral`, `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |

2306	## Browsers
2307	
2308	The sandbox starts one browser unless `agent.json` asks for more, up to four:
2309	
2310	```json
2311	{"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "browsers": 3}
2312	```
2313	
2314	`browsers` is a whole number from 1 to 4; anything else rejects the package with
2315	`Invalid agent.json: browsers: must be a whole number from 1 to 4`. Browser n is its own headful Chromium with its
2316	own profile, on display `:n` (1280×800) with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9221 + n (9222 to 9225), behind
2317	the same proxy as browser 1. All of them are ready before the clock starts. `CDP_URL` stays browser 1, `CDP_URLS` lists all of
2318	them in order, and `BROWSER_COUNT` says how many there are. With three:
2319	
2320	| Variable | Value |
2321	| --- | --- |
2322	| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222` |
2323	| `CDP_URLS` | `["http://127.0.0.1:9222","http://127.0.0.1:9223","http://127.0.0.1:9224"]` |
2324	| `BROWSER_COUNT` | `3` |
2325	
2326	**At most 4 browsers run at a time:** ask for up to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts
2327	inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The scored sandbox enforces it:
2328	any other browser the agent starts is stopped within seconds, and the run's logs say so with
2329	`[platform] stopped a browser the agent started: at most 4 run at a time; use the browsers from CDP_URLS`. Every
2330	browser then is one the platform can show and record: test runs show them side by side while they run, with a
2331	recording of each afterwards.
2332	
2333	On your own machine, developing with the scouting logins, `CDP_URLS` is not set and your agent starts its own
2334	browsers.

2340	# Building your agent
2341	
2342	Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
2343	the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
2344	model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
2345	checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
2346	script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
2347	websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
2348	
2349	## The browser
2350	
2351	In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
2352	`127.0.0.1:9222`.
2353	
2354	- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
2355	- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
2356	  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
2357	- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
2358	  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.
2359	
2360	### Several browsers
2361	
2362	To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:
2363	
2364	```json
2365	{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
2366	```
2367	
2368	Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
2369	order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:
2370	
2371	```javascript
2372	import { chromium } from "playwright"
2373	
2374	const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
2375	const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
2376	const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
2377	await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
2378	```
2379	
2380	At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
2381	inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
2382	them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
2383	of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.
2384	
2385	## Models
2386	
2387	The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
2388	OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
2389	pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
2390	[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
2391	up.
2392	
2393	## What makes it hard, on purpose
2394	
2395	The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
2396	that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
2397	"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
2398	every page as adversarial and verify what you read.
2399	
2400	## Tips
2401	
2402	- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
2403	- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
2404	- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
2405	- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
2406	- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
2407	  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
2408	- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
2409	- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
2410	  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
2411	  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
2412	- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
2413	  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
2414	- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
2415	
2416	## Starter kit
2417	
2418	[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
2419	submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
2420	Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.
